segments.he: אָמַר: בְּ"הוֹדוּ" שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת קדֶם מִנְחָה יְכוֹלִין לְשַׁבֵּר לִבּוֹ מְאד וּלְפָרֵשׁ כָּל שִׂיחָתוֹ שָׁם כִּי שָׁם מְדַבֵּר מֵעִנְיַן צָרוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וּמֵעִנְיַן צְעָקָה עַל כָּל דָּבָר (שָׁם, סִימָן ע"ר) .
segments.en:
The Psalm recited before Sabbath is an    opportunity to really articulate oneself

He said: In “Hoadoo” (“Praise” - Psalms 107) which is said before Sabbath, before mincha (-the afternoon prayer), it is possible to break one's heart very much, and to express all one's words there, because it speaks there regarding the  hardships of the soul and regarding screaming (to Hashem) over every matter. (Words of Rabbi Nachman, article 270).
